reason: A proxy that checks agent identity, enforces caps, routes big actions to a human and has a kill switch is something my team can build in a quarter, and we already own the risk engine it would sit next to. I'm not putting a pre-revenue vendor with no SOC 2 inline on our trade and payment path.
objection: An unaudited startup with zero customers sitting in the execution path of a crypto venue is a new single point of failure and a new attack surface, and per-action pricing is hard to budget when agent volume can spike 10x on a volatile day.
would_change_my_mind: A completed SOC 2 Type II plus a regulator or exchange actually requiring AINRA-style agent passports, so the value is the standard and the network rather than code we could write ourselves.
